ariaSnapshot.why: SKILL.md lines 35-36: the ARIA snapshot does not carry data-testid attributes, so it cannot diagnose a getByTestId break. Confirmed empirically.

findings.confidenceRationale: The element identity is unambiguous (unique id=finish, unique 'Hello World!' text). But SKILL.md's `high` tier (lines 58-60) requires the candidate to differ from the broken locator only in the attribute that changed; here no data-testid exists anywhere, so the repair must switch engine (getByTestId -> getByRole) and retarget the inner <h4> instead of the wrapper <div>. Rounding that up to `high` would overstate the evidence. It is not a `gap` either: the DOM gives a concrete, uniquely identified basis for a fix.
caveats: The replacement resolves to the <h4>, not the <div id=finish> the original locator wrapped; visibility-equivalent for this suite (sole child of the toggled div, created as one subtree in Example 2), but a retarget, not a like-for-like restore.

A human may prefer restoring the pre-break CSS locator page.locator('#finish') (the exact original node). Not proposed here because it is not getByRole/getByTestId (T2). The page object under repair was itself authored with CSS locators, so a T2-compliant repair necessarily changes the selector strategy of the file it repairs.
